description: Create the complete thesis defense presentation HTML file at /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html. This is a single-file, self-contained HTML presentation about 'Direct Visual Servoing Using Multiscale Decomposition' with 11 slides, inline CSS, and inline JavaScript. Then apply two modifications: (A) stunning robot arm power-on animation in slide 2, and (B) distinct individual colors for tag buttons.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html with a complete, professional thesis defense presentation containing: DOCTYPE html, lang='en', full head with meta charset/viewport, title 'Direct Visual Servoing Using Multiscale Decomposition - Thesis Defense', inline <style> block, 11 slides in the body, and inline <script> at the end.

SLIDE STRUCTURE: Create 11 slides as sections/divs. Slide 1 (id='slide-1'): Hero/title slide with title 'Direct Visual Servoing Using Multiscale Decomposition', subtitle, author name placeholder, university info, and a div with class 'hero-tags' containing 4 span.tag elements: 'Visual Servoing', 'Multiscale', 'Robotics', 'Computer Vision'. Slide 2 (id='slide-2'): 'General Context' with a robot arm SVG diagram. Slides 3-11: Various content slides covering Introduction, Problem Statement, Methodology, Multiscale Decomposition, Visual Features, Control Law, Experimental Results, Comparison, and Conclusion/Q&A. Slide 11 should have a div with class 'seq-s11-tags' containing 4 span.tag elements summarizing contributions.

SLIDE 2 ROBOT ARM SVG: In slide 2, include an inline SVG diagram of a robot arm with these elements: a base platform (class 'gc-robot'), vertical link from base to J1 joint, J1 joint circle, link from J1 to J2, J2 joint circle, link from J2 to J3, J3 joint circle, link from J3 to end-effector, and a camera element at the end-effector (class 'gc-camera'). Include FOV (field of view) lines from camera (class 'gc-fov-line'). Give each segment group IDs for animation targeting (e.g., 'robot-base', 'robot-j1-link', 'robot-j1-joint', 'robot-j2-link', 'robot-j2-joint', 'robot-j3-link', 'robot-j3-joint', 'robot-camera').

CSS BASE STYLES: Include full presentation CSS - dark/professional theme background (dark navy/charcoal gradient), white/light text, slide transitions, navigation arrows, progress indicator, smooth font (Inter or system fonts). Each slide should be full viewport height. Include .slide class for each section, .active for current slide, transitions for slide changes.

CSS TAG MODIFICATION (B): Instead of a single gradient for all .tag elements, use nth-child selectors to give each tag a distinct color. Apply to both '.hero-tags .tag' and '.seq-s11-tags .tag': nth-child(1) gets deep blue background (#1e40af), nth-child(2) gets emerald green (#059669), nth-child(3) gets amber/gold (#d97706), nth-child(4) gets rose (#be185d). Keep white text color, padding (0.5em 1.2em), border-radius (2em), font-weight bold, and a subtle box-shadow for each.

CSS ROBOT ANIMATION (A) - STUNNING POWER-ON SEQUENCE: Add elaborate @keyframes animations that make the robot arm 'power on' and come alive when slide 2 is active. Requirements: (1) Each segment animates sequentially with staggered animation-delay - base first, then J1 link, J1 joint, J2 link, J2 joint, J3 link, J3 joint, camera last. Use different effects per segment: base slides up with scale, links extend/grow from their origin point, camera fades in with a scale pulse. (2) Glowing energy pulse effect: Create a @keyframes 'energyPulse' that animates a glowing stroke or filter along the arm segments (like electricity flowing through). Use stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset animation on the links, plus a drop-shadow glow filter that pulses. (3) Joint glow: The J1, J2, J3 joint circles get a @keyframes 'jointSpin' with rotating box-shadow/drop-shadow that creates a spinning glow ring effect, plus a scale pulse. (4) Camera lens focus: The camera element gets a @keyframes 'lensFocus' with a pulsing scale and alternating glow intensity to simulate focusing. (5) Particle/spark effects: Add pseudo-elements (::before, ::after) on the joint elements with small dot/spark shapes that orbit or scatter using @keyframes 'sparkOrbit'. These should be small glowing dots that rotate around the joints. (6) The entire robot group should also have a subtle @keyframes 'breathe' animation (very gentle scale oscillation) once fully powered on. (7) All animations should only play when the slide is active - use a selector like '#slide-2.active .gc-robot' to trigger them. Initial state should be opacity:0 or transform:scale(0) so nothing shows until animated.

JAVASCRIPT: Add inline script at the end of the body that handles: keyboard navigation (arrow keys, space), click/touch navigation arrows, slide transition logic (add/remove .active class), progress bar update, and a canvas-based particle background animation (subtle floating particles in the background for visual appeal). The script should set slide 1 as active on load.

FINAL POLISH: Ensure all 11 slides have meaningful content related to visual servoing thesis topics. Add smooth transitions between slides. Make sure the presentation looks professional and impressive for a thesis defense. The particle background should be subtle and not distract from content.
acceptance_criteria: presentation.html exists and is valid HTML5 with all 11 slides
Slide 2 has id='slide-2' with a robot arm SVG containing identifiable segments (base, links, joints, camera)
CSS contains @keyframes animations for robot power-on: sequential segment animation, energy pulse on links, joint spinning glow, camera lens focus pulse, and particle/spark pseudo-elements on joints
Robot animations only trigger when #slide-2 is active (via #slide-2.active selector or similar)
Tag colors use nth-child selectors giving each tag a distinct color (blue, green, amber, rose) instead of a shared gradient
JavaScript handles slide navigation (keyboard + click) and particle background
The file is completely self-contained (no external dependencies except optionally Google Fonts CDN)
verification: Run: python3 -c "from html.parser import HTMLParser; HTMLParser().feed(open('/projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html').read()); print('HTML parsing OK')" to verify valid HTML
Run: grep -c '@keyframes' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm multiple keyframe animations exist (should be >= 5)
Run: grep -c 'nth-child' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm nth-child selectors for tags (should be >= 4)
Run: grep 'slide-2' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm slide 2 exists with robot content
Run: grep -c 'gc-robot\|gc-camera\|gc-fov' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm robot SVG elements exist
Run: grep 'hero-tags' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm hero tags section exists
Run: grep 'seq-s11-tags' /projects/sandbox/Scriptemedd/presentation.html to confirm slide 11 tags section exists
findings: All verification checks passed. HTML valid, 11 slides confirmed, 10 @keyframes animations, 4 nth-child tag color selectors, robot SVG with gc-robot/gc-camera/gc-fov-line classes, hero-tags and seq-s11-tags present, JS navigation and particle canvas working. Post-review fix applied: replaced all '%%' with '%' in CSS (Python format-string escaping had leaked into the output), and added transform-box: fill-box + transform-origin: center to .spark rule for correct SVG orbit animation.
